root_cause.text: In MPTCP `__mptcp_retrans()` the fallback path could still trigger packet reinjection while holding `msk->fallback_lock`, and `__mptcp_try_fallback()` would try to take the same lock again, creating a recursive-lock deadlock during fallback/infinite-map handling.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says “The packet scheduler could attempt a reinjection after receiving an MP_FAIL and before the infinite map has been transmitted,” and the patch changes `__mptcp_retrans()` to skip retransmission when fallback is active by adding `|| !msk->allow_subflows` with the comment that “we can't retrans even when an infinite fallback is in progress,” directly preventing the double-lock on `msk->fallback_lock`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE says “The packet scheduler could attempt a reinjection after receiving an MP_FAIL and before the infinite map has been transmitted,” and the patch changes `__mptcp_retrans()` to skip retransmission when fallback is active by adding `|| !msk->allow_subflows` with the comment that “we can't retrans even when an infinite fallback is in progress,” directly preventing the double-lock on `msk->fallback_lock`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent retransmission when MPTCP subflows are disabled, including during infinite fallback.
intent_record.what: In __mptcp_retrans(), the comment above the fallback-atomic section was expanded, and the conditional under fallback_lock was changed from `if (__mptcp_check_fallback(msk))` to `if (__mptcp_check_fallback(msk) || !msk->allow_subflows)`, causing the code to exit early when subflows are not allowed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, retransmission is now skipped not only when fallback is detected, but also when the MPTCP socket is in a state where new subflows are disallowed, preventing retransmit work during an infinite fallback condition.

grouping_result.intent: Prevent retransmission when MPTCP subflows are disabled, including during infinite fallback.

relevance_review.reason: The change explicitly targets preventing retransmission in the MPTCP fallback/infinite-fallback path, which matches the root cause involving reinjection/retransmission while holding fallback_lock and the resulting recursive-lock deadlock.

candidates.rationale: This lock is taken to make retransmission and fallback decisions atomic. The root cause is that the fallback path could still trigger reinjection while this lock was already held, and __mptcp_try_fallback() would attempt to lock it again, causing recursive-lock deadlock.

This fallback check is the decision point that can lead into the fallback/infinite-map path. In the vulnerable flow, this branch could proceed into retransmission/reinjection while the fallback lock remained held.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement acquires fallback_lock before entering the retransmission/fallback decision path. In the vulnerable flow, retransmission could still reach fallback handling while this lock was held, and __mptcp_try_fallback() would try to take the same lock again, causing recursive-lock deadlock.

This branch is the decision point that can enter the fallback/infinite-map path while fallback_lock is already held. That allows reinjection/retransmission to proceed into code that may re-acquire the same lock, triggering the deadlock described in the root cause.
